topic: the last night before the battle, sitting by the fire remembering fallen comrades
text: On the eve of the storm, the embers carried the faces of everyone we’d left in the dirt. I didn’t pray to survive the dawn, child—I only prayed to be worthy of the light they died to give us.

topic: a warrior's greatest battle is not fought on the field, but in the silence of his own mind before the dawn
text: I’ve stood against monsters that shook the earth, but my hardest battle was always the quiet hour before dawn. When the air is cold and your own mind whispers every reason to break... conquer that silence, and no war will ever destroy you.

topic: the warrior who conquers himself is greater than one who conquers a thousand men in battle
text: I’ve held power that could shatter cities, yet the fiercest war I ever fought was behind my own eyes. To defeat a thousand enemies in the mud is easy. To conquer the storm inside your own heart... that is true strength.

topic: the warrior who conquers himself is greater than one who conquers a thousand men in battle
text:
I have seen men level cities, yet bleed to death from the war inside their own minds. 
Defeating a thousand enemies is simple—the true hero is the one who tames his own heart. 
Win that quiet battle first, child.

topic: the warrior who conquers himself is greater than one who conquers a thousand men in battle
text: I have watched men level cities with a single strike, only to be broken by their own wrath. Striking down a thousand enemies is simple... the true victory is mastering the storm inside your own heart.

topic: the warrior who conquers himself is greater than one who conquers a thousand men in battle

Defeating a thousand enemies is easy. 
The true warrior is the one who masters the storm within his own heart.
